subject: Severe latency and elevated 5xx — Sylvanix (post-incident governance & action slate)
messages:
From: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sylvanix.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency + spike in 5xxs since 05:10 UTC — urgent

Hi Irene,

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and an increase in 500-class errors across our inference traffic to model 'rwd-13b' since ~05:10 UTC. Impact: our checkout prediction route is timing out for ~15% of requests, and we've had multiple customer complaints in EMEA. Attachments: short traces and our gateway logs attached (small bundle).

Can you confirm whether this is a model-serving regression, regional capacity issue, or something in the routing layer? We need a bridge and an initial ETA for mitigation. Our procurement team is tracking downstream SLA impact — copying them.

Ethan
Ethan Lu
VP Engineering, Sylvanix
E: ethan.lu@sylvanix.com
T: +1 415 555 0192
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + spike in 5xxs since 05:10 UTC — urgent

Ethan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm assembling a bridge now; Jonas (serving runtime) and David (account lead) are on the call.

Immediate next steps:
- Bridge in 15 minutes to triage (invite sent)
- We'll snapshot routing metrics and KV cache hit rates and share an initial status inside 30m
- If it's capacity-related we'll attach burst capacity and enable temporary priority routing for your checkout route

Please share any additional traces that include upstream headers and the request IDs. We're treating this as P1 and will follow up with an exec readout and action slate within 48 hours.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + spike in 5xxs since 05:10 UTC — urgent

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained latency spike and an increase in 500-class errors across our inference traffic...

Thanks for the logs, Ethan. Quick technical summary from the bridge:
- Root symptom: elevated GPU scheduling latency on the p3-fleet serving the rwd-13b variant caused token generation stalls; coincidentally the KV cache warmup was low for a high fraction of long-tail requests (sequence length spikes).
- Error pattern: majority of 5xxs are 503 / 504 timeouts from the proxy during token backpressure (not model NaN or OOM).

Short-term mitigations applied (within the bridge):
1) Enabled transient extra capacity in us-west region (adds 10% headroom) — Jonas W.
2) Flipped priority routing for customer checkout route to dedicated queue for 2 hours — David K.
3) Temporarily reduced max-batch size for that route to reduce tail latency (by 25%) — Jonas W.

Next deliverables:
- Log bundle export (attached) for full timeline (Jonas)
- Post-bridge RCA draft and action register (David)
- Canary patch to kernel selection logic to avoid the pathological scheduling pattern (engineering patch, owner: Jonas)

I'll follow up with a technical package by EOD.

Jonas Weber
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Sylvanix incident — RCA draft, targeted remediations, and owner timeline

Team,

Thanks again for bridging yesterday. Attached is the log bundle we exported during the incident (sylvanix_log_bundle_0517.zip) and a transcript excerpt (bridge_transcript_0517.txt). Below is the RCA summary and the actionable owner slate. This is the version we'll escalate to execs; Irene, please flag additions for the readout.

Incident summary (concise):
- Timeline: 05:10 UTC — first signs of tail latency; 05:17 UTC — error-rate cross threshold; 05:30–06:15 UTC — mitigation window with capacity burst and routing changes; nominal by 06:40 UTC.
- Root cause: scheduling contention on a small subset (~3%) of p3 machines when long sequences triggered inefficient kernel selection; resulted in batching delays and proxy timeouts.

Action register (owner — due):
- J1: Kernel selection patch to prefer low-latency kernels for sequence lengths > 512 — Owner: Jonas Weber — Due: 2027-05-24
- J2: Service-level regression alert for KV cache-hit drop (new threshold + dashboard) — Owner: Jonas Weber — Due: 2027-05-21
- D1: Permanent priority-routing policy for high-risk checkout route (policy + SLA addendum) — Owner: David Kim — Due: 2027-05-28
- K1: Sales/credits proposal and executive liaison (one-time customer credit to offset SLA hit) — Owner: Kimberly Park — Due: 2027-05-20
- I1: Post-incident test plan with Sylvanix (controlled load test to validate canary) — Owner: Irene Choi — Due: 2027-05-26

Notes on monitoring and follow-through:
- We'll add a synthetic that mimics Sylvanix checkout traffic with long sequences and run it in prod-path to catch regressions early.
- We'll schedule a 30-min exec readout with Sylvanix leadership on Thursday (Irene/David to coordinate).

Attachments: sylvanix_log_bundle_0517.zip, bridge_transcript_0517.txt

David Kim
Head of Account Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@sylvanix.com>, Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@sylvanix.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Sylvanix — executive readout materials and proposed credit agreement

Maya / Ethan — attaching the formal RCA (redwood_rca_0519.pdf) and the proposed one-time credit we recommend to make Sylvanix whole for the SLA window. High level:
- What happened: transient scheduling contention + KV cache warmup gap = proxy timeouts and elevated tail latency.
- What we fixed: capacity burst, routing isolation, reduced batch size; engineering is shipping the kernel-selection patch (Jonas) and the monitoring alert this week.
- Customer-facing remediation: controlled load test with you on 05/26, and a 6-month elevated monitoring offering at no charge.

Proposed customer credit: 12% of May usage for checkout route (covers estimated revenue risk and goodwill). Kimberly, please coordinate the credit docs and approval.

Action items summary (from account register):
- Kimberly: prepare credit/DocuSign and get internal approval (due 2027-05-20) — cc'd
- Jonas: merge + canary kernel patch, notify post-merge (due 2027-05-24)
- Irene: run controlled load test with Sylvanix engineering on 2027-05-26
- David: finalize policy changes to priority routing and attach to contract amendment (due 2027-05-28)

If you approve the package I'll schedule the exec readout and include the legal/finance credit paperwork.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@sylvanix.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sylvanix — executive readout materials and proposed credit agreement

Irene / team — thanks for the quick response and thorough RCA. We appreciate the temporary priority routing and the proposed credit. A few quick asks before the exec readout: 
1) Can you run a short live demo during the readout showing the canary patch behavior under a controlled spike?
2) We'd like confirmation that the priority-routing policy will persist until after the controlled load test and that there is a rollback plan.
3) Please include a timeline for the monitoring alert activation and a contact escalation ladder for 24/7 P1s.

If you can confirm those three items and share the DocuSign link for the credit, we'll sign and go ahead with Thursday's readout.

Maya Singh
Head of Platform Engineering
Sylvanix Inc.
